output.summary: KEP-3203 proposes a periodically auto-refreshing, machine-readable feed of official Kubernetes CVEs, implemented by labeling related closed issues or PRs with the "official-cve-feed" label via automation. Status is implementable, stage beta.
output.rationale: Users cannot currently filter issues or PRs related to Kubernetes CVEs, and there is no single place to programmatically fetch fixed CVEs. The KEP addresses this by automatically labeling in-scope issues (closed, with a CVE ID, officially announced by SRC). Triage and disclosure remain with SRC, and CVEProject integration is out of scope for now.

alternatives.option: Use existing CVE data sources (current options)
alternatives.why_not: The readme states current options are either broken or incomplete, which is the motivation for the KEP.
The readme says it may happen at a future stage but is currently not planned or scoped.

alternatives.option: Listing CVEs found in build-time dependencies and container images in the feed
alternatives.why_not: The readme lists this as a non-goal; only official CVEs announced by the Kubernetes SRC are published in the feed.

evidence.quote: This KEP addresses this concern by labeling these issues or PRs with the new label **official-cve-feed** using the automation.
there is no single place for the end users of Kubernetes to programmatically subscribe or pull the data of fixed CVEs.
Only official CVEs announced by the Kubernetes SRC will be published in the feed.
Integration with [CVEProject](https://github.com/CVEProject/cvelist) may happen at a future stage but currently is not planned or scoped.
